corrections.was: Five tabs sit across the top of a Blender window. A Workspace is a saved arrangement of editors for one job, picked from those tabs. The tabs change which editors you see, not the scene. Here the tabs light in turn and stop on Animation, with three editors on screen. For example, to lay out the image on a crate you switch to the UV Editing workspace, and to set up its material you switch to Shading, and the crate itself never changes.

corrections.why: The slide's note says the layouts drawn are simplified; Blender's default window has more workspace tabs than the five drawn, so the sentence must describe the drawing, not Blender.

corrections.was: A table of a pole's numbers. Apply transforms bakes position, rotation and scale into the mesh and resets them to neutral. This pole is a two metre cube scaled to zero point one, zero point one, zero point nine. After apply, the scale reads one, one, one, and the mesh is one point eight metres tall. Scale is a multiplier, and size is the real dimensions. For example, apply a pole's scale before export, so a collider built from it is not stretched.

corrections.was: Blender's axes beside Godot's. Right-handed, plus Z up, is how Blender sets its axes. Right-handed means X cross Y gives Z, and Z points up. Godot is right-handed too, but puts plus Y up, as glTF does. The exporter's plus Y Up option moves the post's one point eight Z extent onto Godot's Y, so it stands. For example, a checkpoint post is tall along Blender's Z, and if it arrives lying on its side in Godot, the plus Y Up option was off.

Godot is right-handed too, but puts plus Y up, as glTF does. The exporter's plus Y Up option moves the post's one point eight Z extent onto Godot's Y, so it stands. For example, a checkpoint post is tall along Blender's Z, and if it arrives lying on its side in Godot, the plus Y Up option was off.
corrections.why: As spoken, 'Z points up' read as part of what right-handed means; handedness and the up axis are separate (Chapter 3: Godot is right-handed and Y-up), so Z up is tied to Blender.
